## Execution and integrity plan

1. Original bytes, SHA-256 inventory and staged/unstaged patches were saved outside Git before edits. Originals selected for archival move with `git mv`; no deletion, commit or push is authorized.
2. Use existing `docs/archive/2026-10-27_cleanup/`, preserving repository-relative paths. Keep small historical redirect pages at moved Markdown report locations so immutable decisions/contracts and old links still resolve. Removed skills receive no discovery stub; supporting references move with their skill. Redirects contain provenance navigation only and cannot restart old tasks.
3. Archive pre-refactor rule/skill snapshots separately, preserving upstream metadata/licence/provenance. Update only evidence-backed current instructions; preserve all trap IDs, contract IDs and acceptance limits. `skills-lock.json` remains unchanged upstream provenance, not an installed-skill census.
4. Consolidate unresolved/carried findings in `docs/BACKLOG_FROM_AUDITS.md`; native 971 unverified contracts, owner/TalkBack/real-file/release gates are not closed by cleanup. Read original evidence through its canonical register when required.
5. Check every move/snapshot SHA-256, active Markdown reference regressions and references to removed skills, instruction frontmatter/names/fences, rule/skill length, whitespace, unchanged application/configuration inputs and preserved dirty content. V1 documentation-only checks apply; no application suite is needed because executable sources/configuration do not change.
6. Keep archive originals byte-identical. Their relative references retain original source coordinates; the archive index maps original paths to archived paths and current successors. Use the original-path redirect or index when reading historical references.
